summary: Arnold J. Toynbee worked in history and archaeology after studying at Winchester College (~1902–1907) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1907–1911). He held posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arnold Kunst worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, Stanisław Schayer at the University of Warsaw (PhD 1930–1934), and Erich Frauwallner at Vienna. He held posts at Lviv, Cambridge, and SOAS.

Arsène Darmesteter worked in linguistics. He studied at INALCO, École des chartes, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Gaston Paris. He held posts at EPHE (1872–1877), University of Paris (1877–1882), École Normale Supérieure (1878–1888), and Séminaire Israélite de France.

Artemij Keidan is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed his PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (2001–2005). He served as Lecturer of Russian Language at the University of L'Aquila (2009–2010) and became Associate Professor at Sapienza in 2020.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen, Friedrich Max Müller at Oxford, and Rudolf von Roth at Leipzig. He held appointments at the University of Oxford, including Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1880–1899).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling and at Balliol College, Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office and was a lecturer at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Johannes Edvard Lehmann, and under Friedrich Carl Andreas. He served as Docent at Copenhagen (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bedford School and King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1860.
Arthur Evans was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. He studied at Harrow School (~1865–1870) and Brasenose College (1870).
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied under Annemarie Schimmel. He held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He held faculty posts at Stanford University (1947, 1958) and Yale University (1959, 1961).

Arthur Galletti was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cheltenham College (~1890–1895) and Trinity College, Oxford (~1895–1899), and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service (1900–1934).
Arthur Haberlandt was a scholar in history and archaeology who succeeded Michael Haberlandt in 1924 and held a post at the University of Vienna (~1914–1945).

Arthur Henry Ewing worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Washington & Jefferson College, Pittsburgh Theological Seminary, and Johns Hopkins University. He served as director of Christian Boys' Boarding School, president of Ewing Christian College, and fellow at Allahabad.

Arthur Henry Fox Strangways worked in Indology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882) and Berlin University of the Arts (~1882–1884), and served as a schoolmaster at Dulwich College (1884–1886) and Wellington College (1886–1910).
Arthur James Beattie was a linguist who was educated at Montrose Academy, the University of Aberdeen (~1931–1935), and the University of Cambridge (~1935–1938).

Arthur Leslie Saunders was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1882). He held posts in the Indian Civil Service starting in 1880 and at the India Office from 1918 to 1923.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held professorships at SOAS and the Australian National University, alongside visiting roles at the University of Toronto and The Asiatic Society.
Arthur Marshman Spencer was an Indology scholar who studied at Kingswood School and Headingley College.
Arthur Mason Tippetts Jackson was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1885–1888) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1888–1909).
